name: TX-19
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+25 district lean makes the open seat safely Republican
Tom Sell's $2.4M raised plus $1.3M outside support dwarfs Kyle Rable's $46K
Prediction markets price Democratic win odds near 1%
No public polling; outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's 25-point Republican lean, an overwhelming fundraising gap favoring Tom Sell, and market odds near one percent for Democrats leave little doubt despite the open seat and absence of polling.
model.watch: A major scandal involving the Republican nominee or a historic national wave could narrow the margin, though the seat's fundamentals are very unlikely to change.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Jodey Arrington (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Texas's 19th District is among the most Republican-held seats in the country, and even with Jodey Arrington retiring, the open-seat contest strongly favors the GOP. Republican Tom Sell has raised $2.4 million and drawn roughly $1.3 million in outside support, while Democrat Kyle Rable has raised about $46,000 with little cash remaining. Prediction markets put Democratic odds near one percent.

No public polls cover the race, so the outlook rests on the district's 25-point Republican lean and the stark financial gap. The national environment would need to shift historically to make this competitive. Barring an extraordinary development, the seat is expected to remain in Republican hands by a wide margin.
